Package neqsim.process.fielddevelopment.wellplanning

Class WellChemicalTreatment

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.fielddevelopment.wellplanning.WellChemicalTreatment
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class WellChemicalTreatment extends Object implements Serializable
Hydrate-inhibitor (MEG or methanol) requirement along a well using rigorous CPA hydrate equilibrium, phase partitioning of the inhibitor, and injection-rate and pump-duty basis.

For each pressure and temperature station (for example the flowing wellhead, mid-well and tree conditions and the shut-in cold tree) the model finds, by bisection, the inhibitor mass fraction w on the basis of inhibitor plus water such that the NeqSim hydrate formation temperature of the whole fluid (including inhibitor partitioning into gas and hydrocarbon liquid) is at least the subcooling margin below the station temperature. The governing station gives the lean-solution injection rate m_lean = w m_water / (x_lean - w). A TP flash at the station reports the inhibitor split between gas, hydrocarbon liquid and aqueous phase and the aqueous inhibitor concentration.

The fluid must be a CPA system (for example SystemSrkCPAstatoil with mixing rule 10) containing water. The generic chemicalInjectionRateLitresPerHour(double, double, double, double) gives injection rates for scale, corrosion, scavenger and demulsifier doses that are sized with the existing chemistry performance classes.

Limitations: screening; hydrate thermodynamics only (no kinetic inhibitors, no salt-in-MEG solubility or regeneration model); inhibitor injected at the station is assumed mixed with all produced water; no downhole injection-mandrel hydraulics. Validation compares the CPA inhibition effect with the Hammerschmidt correlation and checks mass balances; it is not field-calibrated.
